128c93724417.title: The Memorial Feast for Kökötöy Khan
128c93724417.author: Sagymbaĭ Orozbak uulu
128c93724417.note: Tentative late-medieval to early-modern formation window for the Manas story tradition. The tradition's age is disputed: claims of much earlier origins coexist with arguments for substantial sixteenth–eighteenth-century formation. These rounded bounds are an editorial browsing estimate, not established dates for this episode's first telling. Orozbak uulu's 1920s dictation and the 2022 English edition are later witnesses, not the oral story's origin.

dateLayers.title: Manas / Kökötöy oral tradition
dateLayers.note: Broad, disputed formation estimate. Individual motifs may be older; no exact medieval composition date is known.

5739e0183ff5.title: African Myths of Origin
5739e0183ff5.author: Various / unverified
5739e0183ff5.note: Mixed-age collection, not a work composed in 1800–1970. The displayed span is a broad editorial envelope from ancient Egyptian mythic traditions to later African kingdom traditions. Its endpoints do not date every story or imply continuous composition. Individual traditions are separated below; oral first tellings that cannot responsibly be dated remain explicitly uncertain. The ancient endpoint uses Egyptian mythological attestations as context, not a verified date for every Egyptian story selected by Belcher.

dateLayers.title: Egyptian stories (chapter 20): ancient mythic background
dateLayers.note: Approximate background window: Egyptian mythic narratives are attested from the Pyramid Texts onward. This is a tradition-level anchor, not a dating of each selected tale.

dateLayers.title: Ethiopian royal legends (chapter 21): medieval literary context
dateLayers.note: Approximate medieval context for Solomonic legends, including the Kebra Nagast tradition; the purported age of Solomon is not the composition date. The exact selected-story lineage has not been established.

dateLayers.title: Maninka / Mali origin stories (chapter 64)
dateLayers.note: Tentative early formation window for the Sunjata-related dynastic tradition after the thirteenth-century foundation of Mali; a historical-context inference, not a surviving medieval transcript.

dateLayers.title: Kingdom and people origin traditions
dateLayers.note: Very broad contextual estimate for later dynastic narrative layers, including Kongo and Dahomey sections. Stories may preserve older motifs; kingdom dates do not establish first tellings.

dateLayers.title: Hunter, cattle and trickster traditions
dateLayers.note: Long-transmitted oral material, including San, Eshu, Legba and Ananse traditions. No defensible single origin year or bounded range was established. These stories are not being dated to nineteenth-century collecting.

d53db4ac93e9.title: Sunjata
d53db4ac93e9.author: Bamba Suso and Banna Kanute
d53db4ac93e9.note: Tentative early formation of the Sunjata dynastic epic after the thirteenth-century Mali founder. The upper bound is an editorial allowance for generations of oral development, not a dated manuscript. Modern performances by Suso and Kanute preserve a changing tradition; their recording date does not date its origin.

textDate.label: Modern performances (century only; exact recording dates not verified)

eac8fb6b7a35.title: The Book of Dede Korkut
eac8fb6b7a35.author: Various / unverified
eac8fb6b7a35.note: Broad origin-and-development range for the Oghuz oral stories, with early layers commonly connected to the ninth–tenth centuries and recognisable versions developed by the thirteenth–fourteenth centuries. Scholars differ on these layers. Fifteenth–sixteenth-century manuscripts are later witnesses, not the beginning of the entire tradition.

dateLayers.title: Bamsı Beyrek / Alpamysh-related narrative
dateLayers.note: Approximate early Oghuz oral background; the relationship does not establish an exact first-telling date.

dateLayers.title: Basat and Tepegöz
dateLayers.note: An associated story is attested in an early-fourteenth-century Arabic history. Earlier oral origins are possible.

fec052ffd12e.title: Italian Folktales
fec052ffd12e.author: Italo Calvino
fec052ffd12e.note: Tentative early-modern to pre-collection Italian tale-tradition window, informed by the written fairy-tale lineages of Straparola and Basile and later regional oral traditions. Not a claim that every tale began after 1500 or before 1850: first tellings are generally unknown. Calvino's 1956 literary compilation is retained separately.

b3cc5d2d1712.title: Selected Tales
b3cc5d2d1712.author: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm
b3cc5d2d1712.note: Broad editorial window for medieval and early-modern antecedents of the Grimms' tale traditions, rather than their 1812–1857 editions. The dating varies by tale and does not establish a first telling for each selected story. No prehistoric date is inferred merely from a recurring motif.

169c469a20fc.title: Little Red Riding Hood, Cinderella, and Other Classic Fairy Tales
169c469a20fc.author: Charles Perrault
169c469a20fc.note: Approximate window for recoverable medieval and early-modern tale antecedents through Perrault's versions. Some motifs and international parallels are much older, but resemblance alone does not date the French tale. The individual examples below are attestations and antecedents, not exact oral birth dates.

dateLayers.title: Sleeping Beauty antecedents
dateLayers.note: Medieval Perceforest precursor and Basile's seventeenth-century version precede Perrault.

dateLayers.title: Cinderella: European literary lineage
dateLayers.note: Basile's European prose version precedes Perrault. Older Egyptian and Chinese analogues do not establish when this specific European lineage began.

dateLayers.title: Little Red Riding Hood
dateLayers.note: Earlier oral circulation is likely, but an exact origin range for Perrault's specific story is not established here.

c89eee717bd1.title: Tales of the Greek Heroes
c89eee717bd1.author: Roger Lancelyn Green
c89eee717bd1.note: Broad ancient Greek literary-tradition window for the heroic myths retold by Roger Lancelyn Green. Earlier oral roots cannot be dated individually here. The 1958 retelling is modern; the timeline follows the source stories.

5f3f78b22fef.title: The Ramayana: A Shortened Modern Prose Version
5f3f78b22fef.author: R. K. Narayan
5f3f78b22fef.note: Approximate proposed early formation range of the Rama narrative, encompassing differing scholarly dates for its oldest layers. Narayan's modern prose retelling draws especially on the medieval Tamil Ramayana; neither that adaptation nor the 1972 publication is the origin of the Rama story.

dateLayers.title: Early Rama / Sanskrit epic tradition
dateLayers.note: Approximate disputed early composition range; later books and redactions continued to develop.

dateLayers.title: Kamban's Tamil Ramayana
dateLayers.note: Medieval source adaptation important to Narayan's retelling, not the origin of the Rama narrative.

19f49019b4fb.title: Rama the Steadfast
19f49019b4fb.author: Valmiki
19f49019b4fb.note: Approximate proposed early formation of the Rama narrative. Scholars differ between an early first-millennium-BC oral core and fifth–fourth-century-BC formation; later written redaction is separate. This dates the source tradition rather than a modern translation.

textDate.label: Previously used Sanskrit composition / redaction span

811806c7cd44.title: The Acts of King Arthur and His Noble Knights
811806c7cd44.author: John Steinbeck
811806c7cd44.note: Medieval Arthurian romance tradition underlying Steinbeck's adaptation, from twelfth-century literary development to Malory. This does not use the purported fifth–sixth-century life of Arthur as a composition date. Steinbeck's posthumous 1976 publication is retained separately.

42615f87d0f2.title: Barlaam and Josaphat: A Christian Tale of the Buddha
42615f87d0f2.author: Gui de Cambrai
42615f87d0f2.note: Source narrative develops from Buddhist life-story traditions dated to the second–fourth centuries through Arabic transmission and tenth-century Christian adaptation. Gui de Cambrai's thirteenth-century French poem is a later version; these are story-lineage dates, not dates for his French wording.

dateLayers.title: Buddhist narrative source
dateLayers.note: Approximate date of the Sanskrit source tradition identified in scholarship.

dateLayers.title: Arabic Bilawhar and Budhasaf
dateLayers.note: Eighth-century transmission stage, not a modern translation.

dateLayers.title: Georgian Christian adaptation
dateLayers.note: Tenth-century Christian form precedes the later European versions.

e901e9586485.title: The Classic of Mountains and Seas
e901e9586485.author: Various / unverified
e901e9586485.note: Estimated formation from fourth-century-BC early versions through early Han compilation. Replaces a falsely precise single year of 124 BC; this dates recoverable textual development, with oral mythic roots potentially older.

6e2a9a2351ee.title: Strange Tales From a Chinese Studio
6e2a9a2351ee.author: Pu Songling
6e2a9a2351ee.note: Pu Songling composed and revised these stories from the early 1670s to the early eighteenth century; the 1766 first print edition is posthumous. Older folklore influenced the stories, but does not date Pu's individual literary inventions.
